tracks.label: DELIVER
tracks.title: Extremely Special Delivery
intro: A courier named Fig has opened a delivery firm for things other firms politely leave behind. His first client is a ceremonial pudding. Its rider demands legroom.

missions.title: A Pudding With Standing
intro: Fig owns one cart, two mittens, and a business card longer than the cart. Help him deliver his first awkward promise.

steps.hint: Frostwick Depot: read Fig's pudding order at the side desk.
pages: Order: one pudding to the Candy Sorting staff table. Keep upright. The red crate is flat; the blue crate has a bowl ring. Neither crate contains a passenger.

steps.hint: Candy Sorting: collect the blue bowl crate at the side desk.
pages: You borrow the bowl crate. Someone has written EXECUTIVE SEATING inside its ring. Fig removes the tiny cushion before loading dessert.

steps.hint: Frostwick Depot: choose the pudding crate at the side desk.
pages: The pudding must remain upright in transit. Which crate fits the order?
wrong: The blue crate has a ring that holds the bowl upright. The flat red crate cannot steady it.

steps.hint: Candy Row: choose Fig's delivery style at the side desk.
pages: Fig needs a firm identity. Will parcels arrive with a tiny brass fanfare or a quiet handwritten arrival card? Both include the same careful handling.
outcomes: Fig polishes a pocket horn. It plays one respectable note and one that resembles a wet boot.
Fig buys a pencil and a stack of cards. His first draft says: Your item has reached where you wanted it.

steps.hint: Candy Sorting: deliver the pudding at the side desk.
pages: The staff remove the bowl seal and check the order. Delivery accepted. The pudding has no comment, which Fig enters as complete satisfaction.
The staff request the horn only after the sleeping apprentice wakes. Fig adds ASK FIRST to his fanfare policy.
The staff pin the arrival card over the table. A quiet receipt earns a very loud round of applause.

outro: Fig pays the first fee and crosses out WORLDWIDE on his card. Across Town is already a substantial claim.

missions.title: The Office Goes Upstairs
intro: A Velvet tenant ordered a desk fern. The seller shipped an entire theatrical forest because the invoice said dramatic growth.

steps.hint: Velvet Heights: inspect the fern order at the side desk.
pages: Order: one fern, pot F4, for the lodge reading room. A stage company loaned the other pots. Return those to Candy Row. F4 has a square brass tag.

steps.hint: Velvet Rooftops: inspect the borrowed forest at the side desk.
pages: Three pots crowd the landing: F4 with a square tag, T2 with a theatre mask, and T3 with painted fruit. A stage squirrel asks whether you are its new manager.

steps.hint: Velvet Rooftops: select the reading-room fern at the side desk.
pages: Which pot belongs in the reading room? The order names the pot and its tag.
wrong: F4 has the square brass tag named on the order. The theatre pots must go back.

steps.hint: Candy Row: return the two theatre pots at the side desk.
pages: The stage manager signs for T2 and T3. The squirrel stays with its employer after negotiating a larger acorn allowance.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: deliver F4 at the side desk.
pages: The reader checks F4 and places it beside a chair. Fig resists calling the chair an adjacent lifestyle opportunity.
Fig asks before sounding his horn. The reader requests one tiny note outside the closed reading-room door.
Fig leaves a card that names the pot. The reader uses its blank back to record watering duties.

outro: One fern delivered, two forests returned. Fig adds a cargo count to every future order.

missions.title: A Present for Nobody
intro: A crate addressed to Nobody has circled town. Fig wants to find its person without opening somebody else's gift.

steps.hint: Parcel Palace: read the return label at the side desk.
pages: The return label says Alma at Aurora Signal sent it to the keeper of the empty chair. The archive can explain that phrase. The outer wrapping is intact.

steps.hint: Frostwick Archive: ask about the empty chair at the side desk.
pages: The clerk once waited alone for a signal reply. Alma calls her the keeper of the empty chair. She now works at Aurora Signal. It is a nickname, not a vacant address.

steps.hint: Aurora Signal: resolve the nickname at the side desk.
pages: The crate is for the keeper of the empty chair. Who should acknowledge it before you hand it over?
wrong: The archive identified the nickname as the signal clerk. An odd label does not make a gift ownerless.

steps.hint: Aurora Signal: obtain the clerk's receipt at the side desk.
pages: The clerk confirms the nickname and signs. She opens the gift herself: a second cushion. Alma has embroidered ROOM FOR COMPANY.

steps.hint: Frostwick Depot: close Fig's first delivery ledger at the side desk.
pages: Every strange parcel has a destination and a receipt. Fig gives the regular couriers his fitted crates. Completed ordinary delivery jobs now pay 5 extra Coins.
His pocket horn becomes an optional arrival bell. The clerk books a two-note concert for her lunch break.
His cards become a city receipt pad. The clerk saves the first one beside Alma's note.

outro: The firm is profitable enough for Fig to buy a shorter business card. Nobody receives a dividend. Nobody is not a person on the payroll.

complete: Fig's fitted crates are in service. Each successful ordinary delivery job pays 5 extra Coins.

tracks.label: LISTING
tracks.title: The View Is Negotiable
intro: Nib has been offered a commission on a remarkably affordable rooftop cottage. The photograph contains a chimney, a sunset, and no apparent cottage.

missions.title: An Abundance of Sky
intro: The brochure promises detached living and unlimited headroom. Nib asks you to locate the walls before he orders a ribbon.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: read the cottage brochure at the side desk.
pages: Brochure: Lot 8, roof cottage, forty square paces, private stair. Survey: Lot 8 is a public stair landing. Lot 9 is a storage hut. Neither includes the stair.

steps.hint: Velvet Rooftops: collect the lot markers at the side desk.
pages: Marker 8 stands on an open landing. Marker 9 is attached to a hut. The photographer used the hut's reflection in a polished kettle.

steps.hint: Velvet Rooftops: identify the advertised lot at the side desk.
pages: What is actually on Lot 8, the lot named in the brochure?
wrong: The survey and the marker agree: Lot 8 is the stair landing. The hut stands on Lot 9.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: choose how to correct the brochure at the side desk.
pages: Nib will publish the correction. Choose a plain facts card or a guided tour showing how the photograph misled readers.
outcomes: Nib prints a large lot number and a measured diagram. The sunset receives no square footage.
Nib marks the photographer's kettle position. Visitors may inspect the illusion and then the real boundary.

steps.hint: Velvet Heights: show the correction at the side desk.
pages: The prospective buyer keeps their deposit. They wanted a workshop, and a public stair is an inconvenient place to install a saw.
The buyer uses the facts card to compare a second address. Its plain little diagram becomes more useful than the glossy brochure.
The buyer attends the tour, then teaches a friend the kettle trick. Nib gets applause for explaining his own correction.

outro: No purchase occurs. Nib returns the ribbon and receives a credit for a less ambitious length.

missions.title: The Singing Wall
intro: A second listing promises musical walls. Its tenant would prefer a wall that waits to be invited.

steps.hint: Lantern Flats: hear the tenant's report at the side desk.
pages: The tenant hears humming only when the shop below runs its loose display bell. A tap on the wall alone is quiet. They consent to a visit and ask for a written repair plan.

steps.hint: Brassworks: ask the bell fitter at the side desk.
pages: The fitter can mount the display bell on a padded bracket. Replacing wallpaper will change its pattern, but it cannot stop vibration from the bracket.

steps.hint: Tinsel Toolworks: select a repair recommendation at the side desk.
pages: The noise follows the display bell, and its bracket is loose. Which repair addresses the observed source?
wrong: The loose bracket carries the vibration. A padded mounting addresses that source; wallpaper only covers the wall.

steps.hint: Lantern Flats: record the tenant's repair request at the side desk.
pages: You record the bracket repair and a follow-up visit. Nobody calls a sleeping tenant a demanding demographic.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: update Nib's listing file at the side desk.
pages: The file says: sound reported, source traced, repair requested. It does not claim the repair is complete.
Nib adds a dated repair-status box to his facts card. A box marked pending is much kinder than a false promise.
Nib adds the quiet wall and the running bell to his tour. Visitors can hear the difference instead of trusting his adjectives.

outro: The fitter takes the request. The tenant keeps control of access to their home. Nib retires the phrase acoustic character.

missions.title: A Door for Every Claim
intro: A seller now offers exclusive access to a passage everybody uses. Nib would like one commission that survives a map.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: read the passage offer at the side desk.
pages: Offer: the buyer gets exclusive passage P. The deed sells the lodge pantry only. Map key: dotted lines are public paths; solid boxes are rooms.

steps.hint: Frostwick Archive: inspect the passage map at the side desk.
pages: Passage P is dotted from street to roof stair. The pantry is a solid box beside it. Its door opens onto P, but the room does not swallow the path.

steps.hint: Frostwick Archive: compare the deed and map at the side desk.
pages: What does the offered deed actually convey?
wrong: The deed names the pantry, and the dotted public path remains outside its solid room boundary.

steps.hint: Velvet Rooftops: verify the public stair entrance at the side desk.
pages: A courier and a resident use the stair while you check the posted path name. The seller agrees to remove the exclusive-access claim.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: finish Nib's buyer checklist at the side desk.
pages: Nib trades his commission bonus for a city buyer-service grant. Future property purchases cost 20 fewer Coins. The discount applies when you buy, with no refund on earlier purchases.
His facts cards sit beside every new offer. A child draws a sunset in the margin, carefully outside the floor area.
His honest tours become popular. He opens each by showing the boundaries before showing the flattering kettle.

outro: Nib finally uses his ribbon on the checklist box. It is a modest opening ceremony for a useful habit.

complete: The buyer checklist gives a 20-Coin discount on future property purchases. Earlier purchases are not refunded.

tracks.label: BLOCK
tracks.title: The Block That Stayed
intro: Mrs. Elm has a list of small public repairs. A developer called the list a district transformation package. She called it a pencil and kept writing.

missions.title: A Bench With Neighbors
intro: The market bench has become a snow shelf. Elm wants people to sit down before they are asked to admire anything.

steps.hint: Candy Row: read Elm's bench inspection at the side desk.
pages: The bench frame is firm. Two seat boards split along the grain. The foundry has smooth boards; its gear blanks have sharp teeth. Keep the walking route clear.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: collect the smooth bench boards at the side desk.
pages: Rivet marks two smooth boards for the market. A gear blank looks impressively industrial and exceptionally unfriendly to trousers.

steps.hint: Candy Row: choose the bench surface at the side desk.
pages: Which material belongs on a seat after the frame and boards are checked?
wrong: The smooth boards replace the split seat. Gears have sharp teeth; ribbon cannot bear a sitter.

steps.hint: Candy Row: choose the restored corner's purpose at the side desk.
pages: Elm can fit one notice beside the bench: a sharing shelf for spare goods or a chalk board for neighbor requests. Both leave the path open.
outcomes: A shelf gets two sturdy hooks and a sign: Take what helps. Leave it usable.
A board gets a weather lip and chalk. Its first request is for someone to draw a better sun.

steps.hint: Frostwick: invite the block's residents at the side desk.
pages: Elm asks people what they need before announcing an opening. One neighbor wants a place to wait for a lift. The bench already has its first job.
A neighbor offers clean mittens for the sharing shelf. Elm labels the sizes so nobody has to unfold every pair.
A neighbor writes LIFT TO MARKET beside their name. Another adds a reply and agrees the arrangement directly.

outro: The bench seats three people and a bag of carrots. Elm refuses to count the carrots as a fourth resident.

missions.title: Light on the Steps
intro: The public steps are open, but their lantern points into a window. A bright mistake is still a mistake.

steps.hint: Frostwick: read the steps request at the side desk.
pages: Residents want light on the stair treads. The lamp works; its hood points upward. The bedroom window is above it. Aurora Signal has spare downward hoods.

steps.hint: Aurora Signal: collect the spare lamp hood at the side desk.
pages: The clerk provides a hood whose arrow reads DOWN TO STEPS. She includes fitting instructions and asks you to leave wiring to the fitter.

steps.hint: Frostwick Depot: brief the lamp fitter at the side desk.
pages: The lamp works and the bedroom lies above it. Which direction should the hood send the light?
wrong: The treads need light below the lamp. Point the hood down and shield the bedroom above.

steps.hint: Frostwick: observe the fitted hood at the side desk.
pages: The fitter checks the mounting. You stand on the steps: each tread is visible. The resident checks their window and gives a satisfied wave.

steps.hint: Candy Row: update Elm's repair notice at the side desk.
pages: Elm records the fitter's name and the two views checked. A child draws a lamp that looks suspiciously like a carrot.
The sharing shelf now holds a spare lantern for borrowing. Its card names the person who checks it after return.
The request board gains a completed lamp entry. Elm keeps the request visible beside the result.

outro: The steps are easier to use and the bedroom is darker. Two improvements can share one sensible hood.

missions.title: The Opening That Was Already Open
intro: A sponsor offers a giant arch for the corner. Its legs would stand exactly where the delivery cart turns.

steps.hint: Candy Row: inspect the sponsor's arch sketch at the side desk.
pages: The cart needs a clear gap of four paces. The arch leaves two. A wall banner leaves the full gap. The sponsor insists their name remain readable.

steps.hint: Frostwick Depot: verify the cart width at the side desk.
pages: The foreman shows the cart's four-pace turning template. Folding its handle does not narrow its load. The market needs deliveries after the photographs.

steps.hint: Candy Row: choose the opening decoration at the side desk.
pages: Which decoration keeps the four-pace delivery gap and still displays the sponsor's name?
wrong: The arch leaves only two paces. The wall banner leaves all four and can carry the sponsor's name.

steps.hint: Velvet Heights: agree the sponsor credit at the side desk.
pages: The sponsor accepts the wall banner after Elm adds a clear thank-you line. A small logo can survive without occupying a public footpath.

steps.hint: Candy Row: open Elm's neighbor desk at the side desk.
pages: The corner is ready for daily use. Elm coordinates donation sorting. Each ordinary donation now adds 1 extra Cheer, up to the city limit of 100.
At the sharing shelf, a donated coat reaches someone who asked for that size. The first shelf label is already getting soft at the corners.
At the request board, the first chalk sun is joined by three replies. Elm keeps space for people who arrive after the ceremony.

outro: There is no ribbon across the path. Elm cuts the string around a biscuit tin, which is much more popular.

complete: Elm's sorting desk adds 1 extra Cheer to each ordinary donation, up to 100 Cheer.

tracks.label: RIVALS
tracks.title: The Tin Comets
intro: The Tin Comets wear homemade racing caps and claim to be your most formidable competitors. Their leader, Bea, also asks whether you have had lunch.

missions.title: The Great Wrong Crate
intro: Bea challenges you to find a lost repair kit. Winning means returning the correct kit, which limits several very dramatic strategies.

steps.hint: Brassworks: read Bea's challenge card at the side desk.
pages: Kit K has a triangular latch and three spanners. Kit M has a round latch and paint brushes. The repair shop wants K. Bea takes the north search route.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: inspect the kit crates at the side desk.
pages: A crate with a round latch holds brushes. Under a cloth sits a triangular latch. The Comets' tiny flag has fallen into the cloth.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: identify the repair kit at the side desk.
pages: Which latch identifies the requested spanner kit?
wrong: Kit K has the triangular latch. The round latch identifies the painting kit.

steps.hint: Brassworks: choose the challenge result at the side desk.
pages: You found K first. Claim a solo win, or share credit with the Comets for checking the north route? Bea will keep the result on the club board.
outcomes: Bea records your solo win and asks for a rematch with better crate knowledge.
Bea records a joint recovery. The club board gains your name in an unnecessarily large star.

steps.hint: Tinsel Toolworks: return Kit K at the side desk.
pages: The shop checks three spanners into the kit. You also return the tiny flag. Bea calls this excellent sportsmanship for a terrifying opponent.
Bea practices latch identification for the rematch. She has drawn your winning triangle on her cap.
Bea divides the route notes between both crews. Your giant star now obscures the club's lunch notice.

outro: Nobody takes tools home as trophies. Bea awards a paper spanner, safe for even the least reinforced mantelpiece.

missions.title: A Race Against Bad Labels
intro: The next challenge is a salvage survey. There is no clock. Bea says the time you save by guessing gets spent correcting the guess.

steps.hint: Brassworks: read the salvage survey at the side desk.
pages: Red crosses mean TRAINING ONLY. Plain numbered brass offcuts may enter salvage. Number 6 is plain brass; number 7 bears a red cross. Record the eligible number.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: inspect the numbered offcuts at the side desk.
pages: Number 6 is a clean brass offcut. Number 7 is a cracked pressure part with a red cross and TRAINING stamped below it. Both are heavy enough to look valuable.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: mark the salvage candidate at the side desk.
pages: Which numbered item can the salvage crew accept under the posted rule?
wrong: Only number 6 is eligible. Number 7 is marked for training and must remain separate.

steps.hint: Brassworks Control: ask Dot to check the survey at the side desk.
pages: Dot checks the marks against the inventory. The Comets found the same answer. Two correct surveys still matter when someone later asks what was checked.

steps.hint: Brassworks: compare survey notes with Bea at the side desk.
pages: Bea returns a tray of sound offcuts and leaves the training part in its marked rack.
She announces a draw, then admits she had hoped to beat your triangle cap. You both sign the eligible-item list.
She calls it another joint result and redraws the giant star smaller so everyone can read the notes.

outro: The paper spanner acquires a paper safety sleeve. The rivalry is becoming alarmingly well organized.

missions.title: The Smallest Grand Prix
intro: The Comets want a parade cart for their paper trophies. Their sketch has wheels, a tall sail, and no brake.

steps.hint: Your Garage: inspect Bea's parade-cart sketch at the side desk.
pages: The unpowered cart needs a low load and a working hand brake. A tall sail catches wind. The route slopes toward Candy Row. Rivet will inspect the final design.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: ask Rivet about the cart at the side desk.
pages: Rivet offers a low trophy tray and a checked hand brake. A larger flag can be carried on foot. She will fit the parts after you approve the design.

steps.hint: Your Garage: choose the parade-cart plan at the side desk.
pages: Which plan addresses the slope and the wind?
wrong: Use the low tray and brake. A sail catches wind; a sloping route still needs a brake.

steps.hint: Candy Row: watch the inspected cart demonstration at the side desk.
pages: Rivet tests the brake before the cart joins the route. Bea walks beside it. A paper trophy survives a small bump and becomes a local engineering celebrity.

steps.hint: Brassworks: finish the Comets' club agreement at the side desk.
pages: The Comets share their offcut-sorting jig with the salvage crew. Each successful ordinary salvage job now yields 1 extra scrap.
Bea hangs your solo victory beside the joint survey. She promises a future rematch, then gives you the first biscuit.
Bea hangs the joint recovery beside the survey. Your smaller star fits between everyone else's names.

outro: The Comets keep their caps and their outrageous confidence. They also keep a place for you at the workbench.

complete: The Comets' sorting jig adds 1 scrap to each successful ordinary salvage job.

tracks.label: HATS
tracks.title: The Hat With Two Owners
intro: Two neighbors have claimed the same red hat. One identifies it by color. The other knows what is stitched inside.

missions.title: Inside Information
intro: The hat rests on a public peg. Return it using something better than the loudest claim.

steps.hint: Frostwick: hear the hat claims at the side desk.
pages: Otto says his hat is red. Nell says her red hat has a blue fish stitched inside the brim. Both agree you may inspect the lining.

steps.hint: Frostwick Depot: inspect the hat lining at the side desk.
pages: A blue fish swims through a stitch repair inside the brim. Outside, the hat is simply red. A label reads NELL in letters even Pip can decipher.

steps.hint: Frostwick: return the hat at the side desk.
pages: Whose claim matches the inside fish and the name label?
wrong: Nell described the hidden repair, and the label names Nell. Red alone fits both claims.

outro: Otto remembers leaving his own hat at the soup stall. Nell lends him a spare scarf for the walk. The public peg gets a lost-property card.

complete: Nell has her hat. Otto has a lead and a borrowed scarf. The public peg is available for the next very small mystery.

tracks.label: SOUP
tracks.title: The Soup That Would Not Ring
intro: A cook has ordered a quiet lunch service. Pip has interpreted this as a soup recipe without any noisy vegetables.

missions.title: A Bell Apart
intro: The cook means the counter bell, which wakes a child in the upstairs flat.

steps.hint: Cocoa Corner: read the quiet-service request at the side desk.
pages: The cook needs a visible signal when lunch is ready. The bell must stay silent. A reversible READY card fits the counter; a whistle is even louder than the bell.

steps.hint: Parcel Palace: select the lunch signal at the side desk.
pages: What signals ready soup without making a sound?
wrong: The READY card is visible and silent. Both bell and whistle would make the problem worse.

steps.hint: Cocoa Corner: deliver the READY card at the side desk.
pages: The cook turns the card outward. Three bowls reach three customers. Pip whispers at a carrot until someone gently gives him a spoon.

outro: Lunch continues without the counter bell. Upstairs, a nap survives a complete soup service.

complete: The cafe has a silent lunch card. Pip has learned that quiet service concerns the service, not the carrot.

tracks.label: STAR
tracks.title: A Lease on the North Star
intro: A promoter is selling exclusive views of the North Star. His sign stands under the one awning that blocks it.

missions.title: Open-Sky Inspection
intro: A customer asks whether buying the certificate would move the awning.

steps.hint: Aurora Yard: read the star certificate at the side desk.
pages: The certificate grants a decorative paper star. Its small print grants no land, sky, or exclusive viewing rights. A public overlook is open at Aurora Signal.

steps.hint: Aurora Signal: explain the certificate at the side desk.
pages: What does the certificate actually give its buyer?
wrong: The certificate names a decorative paper star. The public overlook remains open to everyone.

steps.hint: Aurora Yard: correct the star stall's sign at the side desk.
pages: The promoter changes the sign to PAPER STARS, OPTIONAL GLITTER. The customer buys one for their grandchild and walks to the public overlook.

outro: The promoter admits paper stars are easier to keep in stock. The real one remains inconveniently difficult to wrap.

complete: The stall sells what it actually has. The public overlook remains a good place to enjoy things no stall owns.

tracks.label: LANTERN
tracks.title: A Signal for the Biscuit Tin
intro: The signal clerk has secured the biscuit tin with a written reminder. Pip calls it a cipher because that sounds less like being unable to find lunch.

missions.title: Read Before Crumbs
intro: The reminder points to a locker, not a secret emergency signal.

steps.hint: Aurora Signal: read the biscuit reminder at the side desk.
pages: Reminder: the biscuits are in the locker matching the SHAPE of the spare lens box. Ignore its paint. The lens box is triangular and painted blue.

steps.hint: Aurora Core: inspect the lunch lockers at the side desk.
pages: The square locker is blue. The triangular locker is yellow. The round locker is red. Each has its shape embossed beside the handle.

steps.hint: Aurora Core: choose the biscuit locker at the side desk.
pages: The reminder says match shape, not paint. Which locker holds lunch?
wrong: The spare lens box is triangular. Choose the triangular locker even though its paint is yellow.

outro: The clerk opens the triangular locker and shares the biscuits. Pip declares the cipher cracked. Dot labels the tin BISCUITS.

complete: The crew has found its lunch. No public signal was touched in the pursuit of crumbs.

tracks.label: STATUE
tracks.title: The Monument to Almost
intro: A rooftop sculptor has built a snow statue of an important local landlord. It is magnificent from the shoulders up and mostly bucket below.

missions.title: A Lighter Legacy
intro: The sculptor wants to keep the rooftop drain clear while displaying the statue.

steps.hint: Velvet Rooftops: inspect the sculptor's sketch at the side desk.
pages: The drain is at the east corner. The west display pad is clear and level. The snow bucket currently blocks the drain. The sculptor agrees to move it.

steps.hint: Velvet Rooftops: select the statue's display pad at the side desk.
pages: Which location displays the statue while leaving the east drain open?
wrong: The clear west pad leaves the drain at the east corner open.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: report the clear drain at the side desk.
pages: The sculptor moves the snow and bucket to the west pad. Nib photographs the cleared drain first. The landlord asks whether that is his best angle.

outro: The statue gets a label: Temporary Work, Weather Permitting. Its subject considers this an unfairly accurate biography.

complete: The drain stays clear. The snow statue has a suitable place to enjoy its brief career.

tracks.label: CRATE
tracks.title: Please Do Not Wake the Cargo
intro: A parcel on the roof has begun to purr. Its sender insists the contents are a deluxe lap-warming accessory.

missions.title: A Furry Address
intro: The courier asks you to read the care card before anyone decides a crate needs more tape.

steps.hint: Candy Rooftops: read the purring crate's care card at the side desk.
pages: Care card: live cat, name Boots. Keep the air slots open. Deliver to the warm Cocoa Corner, where the owner is waiting. Do not send to the cold storage depot.

steps.hint: Candy Sorting: choose Boots' destination at the side desk.
pages: Which stop is named on the care card and has Boots' owner waiting?
wrong: The care card names Cocoa Corner. The depot is cold storage, and the roof is only a transit stop.

steps.hint: Cocoa Corner: deliver Boots to the owner at the side desk.
pages: The owner checks the name tag and opens the carrier. Boots climbs onto an empty chair and begins inspecting the cafe's lap inventory.

outro: The sender corrects the invoice to LIVE CAT. Boots declines a customer survey by sitting on it.

complete: Boots and the owner are reunited. The carrier keeps its open air slots and loses its marketing copy.

tracks.label: COCOA
tracks.title: A Counter for Cold Hands
intro: Your cafe has customers balancing hot cups beside the door. Build a useful pickup counter without narrowing the entrance.

missions.title: Room for the Next Cup
intro: The project is included with ownership. Nobody needs to buy a premium door-widening subscription.

steps.hint: Cocoa Corner: inspect your pickup-counter plan at the side desk.
pages: The door route needs two clear floor tiles. A deep island leaves one tile. A shallow wall counter leaves two. The carpenter has sound reclaimed wood ready.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: collect the prepared counter pieces at the side desk.
pages: The carpenter has cut a shallow wall top, two brackets, and a rounded edge. The material comes from a dismantled display, checked before reuse.

steps.hint: Cocoa Corner: choose your counter layout at the side desk.
pages: Which layout preserves both clear floor tiles at the entrance?
wrong: The shallow wall counter leaves two tiles. The deep island leaves only one.

steps.hint: Cocoa Corner: check the finished pickup counter at the side desk.
pages: The carpenter secures the brackets. You check the clear doorway and the rounded edge. Completed ordinary jobs now pay 4 extra Coins.

outro: Customers can collect a cup and step aside. The first person to use the counter leaves a neatly folded pair of spare mittens.

complete: Your cafe improvement pays 4 extra Coins per successful ordinary job. No extra project fee was charged.

tracks.label: PARCEL
tracks.title: Every Parcel Gets a Shelf
intro: Your parcel shop has a shelf labeled MISC. It contains everything that should never have met.

missions.title: The End of Misc
intro: Fit a shelf system with readable destinations and a separate space for fragile cargo.

steps.hint: Parcel Palace: read your shelf survey at the side desk.
pages: Rule: fragile boxes go on the low padded shelf. Heavy boxes go low on the plain shelf. The upper rail is for empty bags. A glass ornament is fragile.

steps.hint: Candy Sorting: collect the shelf labels at the side desk.
pages: The sorting crew supplies large-print labels and felt pads. Fig suggests a VIP shelf. You ask whether VIP means Very Insecure Parcel.

steps.hint: Parcel Palace: place the glass ornament test box at the side desk.
pages: Where does the fragile glass ornament belong under the posted rule?
wrong: Fragile cargo goes on the low padded shelf. Weight alone is not its only handling need.

steps.hint: Parcel Palace: finish the shelf check at the side desk.
pages: The shelves are secured and the labels match their spaces. The glass test box stays low on felt. Successful ordinary jobs now pay 6 extra Coins.

outro: MISC becomes an empty label in a drawer. Pip calls it a historic vacancy.

complete: Your parcel shelves pay 6 extra Coins per successful ordinary job. No extra project fee was charged.

tracks.label: TOOLS
tracks.title: A Place for the Useful Bits
intro: Your tool shop has one enormous scrap bin. Finding a washer in it currently counts as a winter expedition.

missions.title: Small Parts, Clear Homes
intro: Fit a sorter that keeps sound offcuts apart from rejected pressure parts.

steps.hint: Tinsel Toolworks: inspect your bin plan at the side desk.
pages: The left tray is marked SOUND OFFCUTS. The right tray is marked REJECTED, DO NOT USE. A drilled brass strip passed inspection. A split valve body failed.

steps.hint: Brassworks Foundry: collect the inspected sorter trays at the side desk.
pages: Rivet supplies two fitted trays and labels with words as well as symbols. She checks the rejected tray has a lid so it cannot mingle with reusable stock.

steps.hint: Tinsel Toolworks: sort the split valve test piece at the side desk.
pages: The valve body failed inspection. Which tray receives it?
wrong: The right tray is marked REJECTED, DO NOT USE. The sound-offcut tray is for pieces that passed inspection.

steps.hint: Tinsel Toolworks: check your completed parts sorter at the side desk.
pages: Rivet verifies both test pieces and closes the reject lid. The sorted sound stock adds 1 scrap to each successful ordinary job.

tracks.label: FLATS
tracks.title: The Landing Belongs to Feet
intro: Your tenants want a warmer common landing. Their first request is to remove the decorative suitcase that nobody can walk around.

missions.title: A Common Place
intro: Make a draft screen and a notice rail while preserving the shared exit.

steps.hint: Lantern Flats: read the tenants' landing plan at the side desk.
pages: The exit swings toward the east wall. The west wall has a fixed alcove beyond the door arc. The screen can fit the west alcove. Nothing may block the exit swing.

steps.hint: Velvet Lodge: collect the fitted draft screen at the side desk.
pages: The joiner provides a screen sized for the west alcove and a slim notice rail. Tenants have approved its position. The suitcase goes back to its owner.

steps.hint: Lantern Flats: choose the screen position at the side desk.
pages: Where can the draft screen stand outside the east door's swing?
wrong: The west alcove lies beyond the door arc. The east wall is inside the exit swing.

steps.hint: Lantern Flats: check the landing with the tenants at the side desk.
pages: The joiner secures the screen. Tenants open the exit fully and walk through. Successful ordinary jobs now pay 3 extra Coins.

outro: The common rail holds repair contacts, a drawing, and a note about a missing suitcase. Its owner adds FOUND before the ink dries.

complete: Your landing improvement pays 3 extra Coins per successful ordinary job. No extra project fee was charged.
